headline: Public exploits for the wp2shell flaws in WordPress core put every unpatched 6.9 and 7.0 site one anonymous HTTP request from remote code execution, as Microsoft warns of a surge in ACR Stealer against enterprises.

emerging_trends.text: Unauthenticated remote code execution keeps landing in the software that runs the open web, and the wp2shell flaws in WordPress core—now carrying working public exploits—leave every unpatched 6.9 and 7.0 site exposed to a single anonymous request.

Credential-harvesting malware is scaling against corporations, with Microsoft flagging a surge in ACR Stealer that lifts browser passwords, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents straight off enterprise machines.

Government agencies are turning commercial data brokers into surveillance engines, and the ICE deal to pay Thomson Reuters $125 million for names, Social Security numbers, and ethnicity data shows how far that reach now extends.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ICE Buys Thomson Reuters Data Trove

topics.title: WordPress wp2shell Exploits Circulate
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer and Help Net Security confirmed on July 18, 2026 that working public exploits now circulate for the two wp2shell flaws—SQL injection CVE-2026-60137 and REST API batch-route confusion CVE-2026-63030—and a persistent-object-cache condition has surfaced that widens the path to code execution on unpatched sites.
topics.summary: wp2shell is a WordPress core bug that runs attacker code from one unauthenticated HTTP request, so a bare install with no plugins is exploitable. Adam Kues at Assetnote reported the REST API flaw; every 6.9 and 7.0 site is at risk until administrators apply the 7.0.2 and 6.9.5 releases.

sources.title: WordPress Core "wp2shell" RCE flaws get public exploits, patch now
Two new high severity WordPress vulnerabilities, patch immediately!
New wp2shell WordPress Core Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code

topics.title: Microsoft Flags ACR Stealer Surge
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft reported July 18, 2026 a surge in ACR Stealer attacks that lift browser-stored passwords, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents from its enterprise customers.
topics.summary: ACR Stealer is a commodity infostealer that harvests saved credentials and session tokens, often arriving through ClickFix copy-paste lures. Organizations should hunt for token theft, rotate exposed secrets, and block the fake-CAPTCHA PowerShell pattern.

sources.title: Microsoft warns of surge in ACR Stealer attacks on customers

topics.title: Fairlife Dairy Production Stays Halted
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported July 17, 2026 that Fairlife's suspended US operation spans plants in Michigan, New York, and Arizona, a Coca-Cola business whose retail sales passed $1 billion in 2022.
topics.summary: A ransomware attack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife dairy subsidiary halted production of its ultra-filtered milk products across the United States. The disclosed plant footprint underscores how one intrusion can idle a billion-dollar consumer supply chain.

sources.title: Dairy company Fairlife suspends production in US after cyber incident

topics.title: Iran Phone Tracking and TKMS Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported July 17, 2026 that Iran tracks the phones of US military personnel, that new CrashStealer malware targets macOS, that attackers exploit OpenClaw AI agents through WhatsApp, and that ransomware struck naval defense builder TKMS.
topics.summary: The roundup ties Iranian device-location surveillance of American troops to a widening set of threats spanning macOS credential theft, AI-agent abuse, and a ransomware hit on a naval defense contractor. Defense-sector operators face pressure to lock down mobile devices, macOS endpoints, and agent integrations.

sources.title: In Other News: Iran Tracks US Military Phones, CrashStealer macOS Malware, CVD Blueprint

topics.title: ICE Buys Thomson Reuters Data Trove
topics.latest_developments: A procurement record surfaced July 17, 2026 shows US Immigration and Customs Enforcement will pay Thomson Reuters $125 million for personal data—names, Social Security numbers, and ethnicity—to investigate what the agency calls "voters fraud" and immigration fraud.
topics.summary: The contract hands a federal enforcement agency bulk access to commercial data-broker records on Americans, sharpening the debate over government surveillance through private data purchases. Privacy advocates warn the ethnicity and identity fields invite profiling.

sources.title: ICE to Pay Thomson Reuters $125 Million to Find 'Voter Fraud'

business.title: Western Pennsylvania Candle Trade Grows
business.latest_developments: TribLive surveyed the region's candle makers July 19 and found a business expanding into new retail storefronts and online shops.
business.summary: Candle makers across Western Pennsylvania are opening storefronts and launching online shops as demand for hand-poured candles climbs, a small-scale manufacturing niche gaining ground in the regional economy.

sources.title: Western Pennsylvania candle makers are on fire

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Library Funding Stays Flat
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 19 that Pennsylvania holds state library aid flat even as branches take on more roles.
around_town.summary: Public libraries across Pennsylvania increasingly serve as community centers, providing internet access, programming, and social services, while state funding for them stays flat, the Post-Gazette reported.

sources.title: Many public libraries in Pennsylvania are evolving into community centers. Why is their funding staying flat?

around_town.title: Lyme Disease Cases Near Records Locally
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported July 19 that Allegheny and Westmoreland counties have already logged more than 1,300 Lyme disease cases this year.
around_town.summary: Allegheny and Westmoreland counties have recorded over 1,300 Lyme disease cases so far in 2026, keeping Western Pennsylvania among the nation's hardest-hit regions for the tick-borne illness.

sources.title: Pa. Lyme disease cases near historic highs in Allegheny, Westmoreland counties

around_town.title: Turnpike, State Police Target Toll Evaders
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported July 19 that a joint April toll-enforcement effort produced more than 200 traffic stops.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission and Pennsylvania State Police ran a joint toll-enforcement initiative in April that led to more than 200 traffic stops, part of a push to collect from drivers dodging tolls.

sources.title: PA Turnpike, state police conduct joint toll enforcement initiative

team_usa.title: IOC Unlikely to Sanction Infantino Over Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian reported July 18 that the IOC will probably take no action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino after a formal complaint over the Balogun red-card affair.
team_usa.summary: United States striker Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card fell away after President Trump phoned Gianni Infantino, and the human rights group FairSquare complained to the International Olympic Committee that FIFA bent its political-neutrality rules under pressure.

sources.title: Gianni Infantino unlikely to face IOC sanctions over Balogun red card scandal
